content:
Notes#JWT#Implemented JWT to the application. My GET endpoints are available to everyone, but my POST, PUT and DELETE endpoints require a special permission, which only Users with the role “admin” have.
Login & Register#Added Login and Register endpoints. Both endpoints needed their own DTO to hold the necessary data for their purpose, and Login generates a JWT token containing their “role”, which determines their permissions. Endpoints that modify data require extra permission, so they check the users permissions before executing.
REST & Test secret#Since I had done my REST-assured tests before implementing JWT (knowing I would later need to update them with JWT), now it was time to do so. I only need an “admin” token to tests my POST, PUT and DELETE endpoints, so I create an “admin” token on test server startup.
However, I had to make a new secret, so my production and test servers don’t share the same. So I generate one in my test class and added it as a parameter to my startServer method, that way the test server uses test secret, my local server uses config.properties’ secret, and my deployed version uses its environment variable secret.
title: JWT, Login & Register

content:
Notes#Atomic#Have added an endpoint that counts the amount of requests my API recieves since it got initiated. This feature was a perfect fit to use Atomic, so it can safely update when several users are modifying (incrementing) it.
This class is made static and is called before any endpoint is accessed, using:
config.routes.before(ctx -> RequestCounter.increment());Then an endpoint was created where we simple get the current amoun, and display it on screen.
Threads#After being unable to use Threads for fetching data form my external API, I was looking for somewhere else to implement it. I decided to make a new endpoint where a few stats about my API would be shown. I created an ExecutorService with a fixed thread pool of 3:
private final ExecutorService executor = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(3);Every thread would fetch some data from my database concurrently, which then would be displayed on the endpoint.
title: Concurrency

Logging#Decided to add the logging logic inside my exceptions, meaning it got implemented in my ExceptionMapping class, and every exception logs accordingly.
Changed the logging behaviour, instead of appending the same file, which will eventually create one huge file, I decided to make the files have a size limit, and upon reaching it, it creates a new file. This gives a better overview and I can delete old files if I wish to do so. This was achieved with:
RollingFileAppender: Switches to a new file when a condition is met. FixedWindowRollingPolicy: Defines what happens when a rollover is triggered. SizeBasedTriggeringPolicy: Defines when the rollover takes place.
title: Exception Mapping & Logging

content:
Notes#Threads#The API I’m fetching exercise data from has 1500 results, which makes fetching them all take some time. To fix this I considered using threads, however it ended up not being possible, due to the api using a cursor based pagination, which means I need the value of the cursor from last call, making using several threads not possible.
Instructions String convertion#The instructions I get from the api is a list of Strings, however, since I see no benefit in that format, I chose to convert it into one single string. Upon running the program, an error ocurred, the instructions were too big for my database column, which was a character varying, which can hold 255 characters. The fix was easy, change the column data to “text”, which I did with: @Column (columnDefinition =“TEXT”)
Http 429 - Too Many Requests#When fetching large amount of data I was getting an error, a http 429 - too many requests. To fix this I added a slight delay between calls, the only downside is the process takes slightly longer.
Exercise Id#Originally I was using the same Ids provided from the external API, which is a mix of numbers and letters. When I started making the endpoint that fetches a specific exercise with its Id, the problem became apparent, I needed a simple and intuitive Id. Adding my own Id to the exercise class fixed this issue, and now the endpoint will fetch the exercise with a given id (fx. id=829).
Enums#Enums were used to avoid typos when searching for specific criteria, and it also provided an “url-ready” string to filter the API.
When I started making my endpoints, specifically my POST endpoint, I wanted to check several attributes, including the input should be found inside these enums, meaning I can’t create a new body part or equipment (willingly or unwillingly), it has to exist in my enums. Now my Enums hold a “value” and a “urlValue”.
“EntityManager is closed”#When fetching a specific ID, since the entity has relations with other entities (tables in the database), I need to trigger Hibernate to fetch that data, because the fetch type is set to lazy. Making Hibernate find the size of those collections, was enough to create the whole Exercise entity with every data from every table.
Pagination#After making the endpoint that fetches all the exercises, I tested it, and it returned one huge list with all 1500 elements. This worked, but wasn’t ideal, and I decided to add pagination, and unlike the API I consumed, which used cursor-based pagination, I would use page-based pagination. To achieve this I changed my getAllExercises() method from my DAO, to now fetch the rows decided by “page” and “pageSize”. I set my page size to be 20, and the user will select the page with a query parameter, which means my endpoint collects the “page” query parameter, and sends it to the method.
title: Threads & My API

content:
Backend#Made ExerciseDTO Created ExerciseMapper Several DAO for exercise fields Notes#ExerciseDTO#Decided to save the data in a DTO instread of the entity itself, respecting SOLID principle. The collections in this class are all of String, that will later be converted to the proper class for the Exercise class (body parts, equipments…etc).
ExerciseMapper#My first thought was to have my ExerciseDAO which would take a list of exerciseDTO and return a list of exercises (from DTO to entity), but this class would also need to interact with the database, which started to feel off, as this class would have more than one responsability. This thought made me create an ExerciseMapper class, that does exactly that, convert exercise DTOs to Exercise entities.
Exercise field DAOs#To better my design, I have tables that contain information about the exercises, such as “target muscle” for example. But many exercises can have that same value, an dthat value can be in many exercises, which describes a ManyToMany relation. These fields have their own table, and in order to convert an exerciseDTO to the Exercise entity, I need to check weather that data exists in my database, if it does, we use the existing row, and if it doesn’t, we create a new row with this new data. This made me create a DAO for every ManyToMany field, where I use a method that either finds the data and uses it, or creates it and uses it.
This definitely made it more complex, but now I have the responsabilities separated.
The API also returns an array of Strings which contain the instructions of each exercise, I converted it to a regular String containing every element instead, since I see no benefit in having it as an array.
title: DTO & DAO

content:
Backend#Implemented API fetching to program Created Enums Notes#API#While creating the API fetching class, I had to take into account my API uses “cursor” pagination, which, once understood, is rather simple, but as it was new to me, I had to learn how it works. I decided to make a method that takes two parameters, a “body part” and “equipment”, so you can search specificly what you are looking for and equipment you have available. While more methods will surely be needed in the future, I decided it was a good start, and I will furthur add methods as I need them, instead of guessing which ones I will need.
A mistake that took me some time to realize, was the url is case sensitive, which gave me inconsistent data. While I knew this, when I fixed the link, and pressed “enter”, my browser used a suggested link I had used before (where case sensitivity wasn’t considered) and wouldn’t work, and it took me some time to realize what was happening.
Enum#A thing I considered, was the method’s inputs would cause problems if they would have a typo. Therefore, I decided to create Enums to store the different options my program accepts, and those Enums are used as parameters. This completely removes the danger of making a typo, and I have more control over what I want my program to be able to fetch.
title: API & Enum

content:
Requirements#Created User Stories for my project, and the Acceptance Criteria for each of the User Stories:
US1 - Create account As a user, I want to create an account, so that I can have my own training data.
- AC 1.1Given I am not logged in, when I enter a valid username and password and submit, then a personal account shall be created.- AC 1.2Given I am creating an account, when I enter invalid data, then I am informed about the issue, the account is not created, and I'm sent back for another attempt.- AC 1.3Given I have successfully created an account, when I log in, then I can access my personal data.US2 - Admin role As an admin, I want to have permission to modify certain data, so that I can keep the app’s data up to date.
- AC 2.1Given I have an admin role, when I log in, then I can modify certain user data.US3 - Create training split As a user, I want to create my own split, so that I can control how my workouts are organized throughout the week.
- AC 3.1Given I am logged in, when I create my split, then I can select the number of days I intend to train per week.- AC 3.2Given I am logged in, when I create my split, then I can give my split a customized name.US4 - Personalize workout As a user, I want to personalize my workouts, so that I can control their names and exercises.
- AC 4.1Given I am logged in, when I've created my split, then I can give my workouts a personalized name.- AC 4.2Given I am logged in, when I've created my split, then I can add execises to a workout.US5 - Select presets As a user, I want to select a preset, a pre-made split with workouts, so that I don’t need to create my own.
- AC 5.1Given I am logged in, when I select to create a split, then I can select to use a preset.US6 - List of exercises As a user, I want to access the list of all exercises, so that I can browse the available exercises.
- AC 6.1Given I am a user, when I select to see all the exercises, then a list appears with all the exercises.US7 - Information about exercise As a user, I want to see information about each exercise, so that I know how to perform them.
- AC 7.1Given I am a user, when I click on an exercise, then information about that exercise will be displayed.US8 - Learn about topics As a user, I want to access information about training topics, so that I can learn and improve my fitness knowledge
- AC 8.1Given I am a user, when I select a topic to learn about, then information about that topic will be displayed.US9 - Quiz about topics As a user, I want to answer a quiz about training topics, so that I can test my knowledge.
- AC 9.1Given I am a user, when I select to answer a quiz about training topics, then a random quiz will be generated.- AC 9.2Given I am a user, when I select an answer to a quiz, then the app will show me the correct answer.- AC 9.3Given I am a user, when I have completed a quiz, then I can select to continue with another.US10 - Track workout As a user, I want to track my performance during a workout, so that I can save my progress.
- AC 10.1Given I am logged in, when I'm tracking my current workout, then I can modify the performance data for each exercise.- AC 10.2Given I am logged in, when I have completed a workout, then I can save the changes.- A 10.3Given I am logged in, when I save my workout changes, then it will be saved for the next time I perform those exercises.US11 - Track weight As a user, I want to track my body weight, so that I can have a history of my weight.
- AC 11.1Given I am logged in, when I select to track my weight, then a field will be displayed for me to enter my current weight.- AC 11.2Given I am logged in, when I select weight history, then a list of all past provided data will be displayed.US12 - See my workouts As a user, I want to view the structure of my current workouts, so that I can have an overview of my workouts.
- AC 12.1Given I am logged in and have created at least one split, when I select to see my workouts, then an overview of my workouts will be displayed.US13 - Workout history As a user, I want to view my workout history, so that I can see the progress I’ve made.
- AC 13.1Given I am logged in, when I select to see my workout history, then past workouts with their data will be displayed.
title: US & AC

content:
Backend#Implemented JPA relations between entities. Implemented LLM as a quiz generator. Notes#Exercise entity had Lists of Strings, which were saved as a @ElementCollection. Under review, learned that could cause multiple instance of the same element, decided to better make them their own tables and utilize their Ids.
Under development, realized my choice of API might not be optimal. Will further research for APIs that better suit my needs.
The quiz LLM works by having a list of subjects, where the promp defines it should select a random subject and generate a quiz. However, under testing, the LLM would pick the first element of the list the vast majority of times. To fix this, an array was created with all the subjects, which was sent inside the prompt, and a random generated value (fitting to the array size) would tell the LLM exactly which element to select. This worked perfectly, however the quiz wasn’t working as intended. The other issue was the correct answer was always placed on the second option. This was fixed with the same logic, a random number (fitting the number of possible answers) was generated, and then injected into the LLM prompt.
Now the LLM properly selects a random subject from the list, and displays the correct answer on a random answer option.
title: JPA & LLM
